instruction: Make all the words in the sight words table bold.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent attempted to color words in a sight-word table by vowel/consonant using Find & Replace with regex. Used wrong colors (yellow, green instead of red/blue) and also colored paragraph text, not just table words. Replaced 28 vowel-starting and 129 consonant-starting matches across the whole document.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open and navigate LibreOffice Writer, use Find & Replace dialog with regex, open Format dialogs to change font properties, use Replace All for bulk formatting changes.
metadata.failure_analysis: Model used incorrect colors (yellow/green instead of red/blue) and applied formatting to all text, not just table cells. The complex multi-step color assignment task exceeded the model's ability to execute precisely.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplified to making table words bold. Model demonstrated ability to select table content and apply formatting. Bold is a simpler property than color (just Ctrl+B). Partial credit supports incremental success.
metadata.explanation: Task requires making all table words bold. Getter counts total and bold words in table cells. Metric gives full credit if all bold, partial credit proportional to fraction of bold words.

scoring_breakdown.partial: N/52 - Proportional credit for N bold words

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly iterates over all tables, rows, cells, paragraphs, and runs to count total and bold text runs in the document's tables, matching the instruction to make table words bold.
Metric correctly returns 1.0 for all-bold, proportional partial credit, and 0.0 for errors or empty tables.
Postconfig properly saves the file (Ctrl+S) before the getter reads it from disk, ensuring state freshness.
Instruction has a single requirement (make all table words bold) which is fully covered by the evaluator.

Minor concern: run.font.bold returns None for style-inherited bold in python-docx. If bold is applied at paragraph/style level rather than run level, the getter may report false negatives. In practice, Ctrl+B in LibreOffice sets bold at the run level, so this should work for the expected workflow.

Minor concern: metric completely ignores the expected parameter (require_all_bold rule is never read). Logic is hardcoded to check all-bold, which is correct for this task but makes the expected config meaningless.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider checking run.font.bold is not False (i.e., True or None with bold style inheritance) instead of strictly requiring run.font.bold == True, to handle cases where bold is inherited from paragraph styles.
Metric could optionally read the expected parameter to respect the require_all_bold flag, making the evaluator more configurable.
